findings.evidence: core.py:34,40,70,90,112,117,202 vs housekeeping.py:62-65,114-143; regexes differ (core.py:35 vs housekeeping.py:63).
findings.fix: Have housekeeping.py import scripts/pr_status/core (share SCOREBOARD_MARKER, the meta regex, TRUSTED_ASSOC, the comment fetch/parse, and the {green,stale} blocking set), or move that shared derivation into core and have core adopt housekeeping's more robust regex, so exactly one copy of the trust/parse logic exists.
findings.issue: core.trusted_comments/scoreboard_meta_from and the review_state blocking check re-derive what scripts/housekeeping.py:114 latest_scoreboard_meta + :143 blocking_rubrics already implement (fetch issue comments, keep <!--tauceti-scoreboard--> markers from OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR authors, take the newest, parse <!--tauceti-meta:v1 ...--> JSON, classify a rubric blocking unless green/stale). The PR presents core.py as the one place that reads PR status yet leaves this parallel copy untouched, and the two have already drifted: core uses r"<!--tauceti-meta:v1 (.*)-->" (literal space, greedy, no re.S) while housekeeping uses r"<!--tauceti-meta:v1\s+(\{.*?\})-->" with re.S, so a multi-line meta parses in one and not the other.

summary: The PR consolidates the labels+Zulip status derivation into core.py, but the advertised single source of truth is incomplete: scripts/housekeeping.py (in-repo, CI-side) independently re-derives the same trusted-scoreboard state, and the two copies have already drifted on the meta regex.
